In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FAD is a useful and powerful tool for the analysis of the structural integrity of RPV and pipeline steels with blunt defects.
the FAD is a useful tool to assess structural integrity of blunt defects in pressure vessels and pipelines.
blunt defects can be assessed in the FAD framework with the same conservatism as for sharp defects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the existing FAD is suitable for assessments of blunted defects.

the FAD is a useful tool for the structural integrity assessment for both sharp and blunt defects, provided that the correct material properties and the actual shape of the defect are taken into account.
blunt defects can be treated with a shape of FAD that is slightly modified to account for the notch geometry and the constraint conditions at the notch tip.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a conservative FAD can be constructed using a single parameter, the notch stress intensity factor, K _{t}.

the shape of the FAF is not affected by the notch radius and that the notch root radius can be used to define margins on failure, i.e. a notch root radius equal to the fracture toughness is sufficient for the assessment of blunt defects.
, in the FAD, the notch driving force (i.e., J -integral) is not a good indicator of the onset of crack initiation, but it is a good indicator of when plastic collapse is dominant.
